name: model-router
description: Cache-aware model and effort routing for Claude Code Desktop: each prompt goes to Haiku, Sonnet or Opus by what it needs, and a cheaper model or effort only when that pays after the prompt-cache re-write. Rules read non-code work too, research is Sonnet at most, !+ and !- nudge the tier, /router-help lists every command, /router why explains the decision, /router-cache shows the cache hit rate and /router-budget caps the spend. Long sessions auto-compact with Haiku at tier thresholds, every prompt you send carries a small model·effort tag, and savings show in dollars and tokens. The hardest tasks can run as Ultracode. Crew mode adds warm per-model workers. Bash output is compressed rtk-style and answers drop the filler.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: route moves the main session to another model when a prompt needs it and the cache math says it pays. crew keeps the main session on one orchestrator model from the first prompt on (its cache is never thrown away) and hands work of several tool calls to long-lived Haiku, Sonnet and Opus workers, each with its own warm cache.

orchestrator.title: Crew orchestrator
orchestrator.description: The model the main session stays on in crew mode.

escalate.title: Harder tasks
escalate.description: auto moves a session to a stronger model when a prompt needs it (or tools keep failing); suggest only names it in the status line.

style.title: Answer style
style.description: terse cuts preamble, recaps and closers; adhd also leads with the next action and numbers steps (after i-have-adhd); off leaves answers alone.

compress.title: Compress Bash output
compress.description: Strips progress bars and passing tests, folds exact repeats, keeps every error line; file contents, diffs and data pass untouched. The last 200 compressed outputs stay whole in ~/.claude/model-router/tee.

useRtk.title: Use rtk when installed
useRtk.description: Hands plain cargo test, pytest, tsc, mypy and go build output to `rtk pipe` when the rtk binary is on PATH; a summary that drops the failures is refused.

cacheTtl.title: Prompt cache lifetime
cacheTtl.description: 1h: Claude Code's default (writes cost 2x input, entries live an hour). 5m: for setups that write 5-minute entries (1.25x). The router's switch math uses it.

judge.title: Judge for unclear prompts
judge.description: haiku asks claude-haiku-5-5 (about $0.0001) when the local rules can't tell. off: no judge; unclear prompts go to laya-serve when layaUrl is set, and otherwise keep the current model.

enableFable.title: Route research to Fable
enableFable.description: Lets proofs, new theories and bounds go to claude-fable-5-1. Turn on only if your plan includes Fable.

showNote.title: Line beneath each answer
showNote.description: A line under each answer naming the model and why, for surfaces with no status line. It also carries the savings: dollars and, when compression or compaction has run, tokens kept out.

promptTag.title: Model tag under your prompt
promptTag.description: Adds a small line like 'router: Opus·medium' to your sent message, so the chosen model and effort sit under what you asked. The turn may still hold or switch for cache reasons; /router why names the final call.

layaUrl.title: laya-serve URL (optional)
layaUrl.description: A running laya-serve (e.g. http://localhost:8000) classifies unclear prompts on your machine for zero tokens, before the Haiku judge.

layaApiKey.title: laya-serve API key
layaApiKey.description: Sent as a Bearer token; leave empty when laya-serve runs without LAYA_API_KEY.

haikuEffort.title: Haiku effort
haikuEffort.description: Base effort when the router moves you to Haiku (on your own model your /effort stays, so its cache stays too). Under effortMode auto a task moves one step from it. Never max or ultracode: the router tops out at xhigh (Extra in Desktop); Ultracode is a separate workflow switch.

sonnetEffort.title: Sonnet effort
sonnetEffort.description: Base effort when the router moves you to Sonnet (on your own model your /effort stays, so its cache stays too). Under effortMode auto a task moves one step from it. Never max or ultracode: the router tops out at xhigh (Extra in Desktop); Ultracode is a separate workflow switch.

opusEffort.title: Opus effort
opusEffort.description: Base effort when the router moves you to Opus (on your own model your /effort stays, so its cache stays too). Under effortMode auto a task moves one step from it. Never max or ultracode: the router tops out at xhigh (Extra in Desktop); Ultracode is a separate workflow switch.

fableEffort.title: Fable effort
fableEffort.description: Base effort when the router moves you to Fable (on your own model your /effort stays, so its cache stays too). Under effortMode auto a task moves one step from it. Never max or ultracode: the router tops out at xhigh (Extra in Desktop); Ultracode is a separate workflow switch.

effortMode.title: Effort per task
effortMode.description: auto picks the effort per prompt within its tier (a confident diagnosis, architecture or security task one step up, a translation or rename one down), taken only when the cache math says it pays, since the cache belongs to model and effort: changing effort rewrites the conversation cache exactly like changing model. task: always take the task's effort, even when the cache rewrite costs more, when effort matters more than the cache. fixed: the tier's effort, as before. The router never sends max or ultracode. Crew workers keep their registered effort.

workerCacheTtl.title: Subagent cache lifetime
workerCacheTtl.description: Claude Code keeps subagent/workflow caches on their own TTL (5m by default), separate from the main conversation. The router uses this TTL for worker reuse math; set 1h only if you also set subagentPromptCacheTtl to 1h.

budgetUsd.title: Session budget (USD)
budgetUsd.description: 0 = off. At 80% the status warns; at 100% budgetAction decides what happens. Measured from the router's list-price ledger, not your plan quota.

budgetAction.title: At the budget
budgetAction.description: warn: only warn. downgrade: move the next task one tier down (never a forced prompt).

compactAuto.title: Auto-compact
compactAuto.description: Past a tier's context threshold the session summarizes with the cheap model, so the expensive model re-caches a short summary instead of the whole transcript. The summary is lossy; /router-compact off disables it for a session.

compactModel.title: Compact model
compactModel.description: The model that writes the summary. haiku is the cheapest and fastest; sonnet keeps more detail.

compactSonnetAt.title: Compact Sonnet at (tokens)
compactSonnetAt.description: Auto-compact a Sonnet session at this context size. 0 disables it for Sonnet.

compactOpusAt.title: Compact Opus at (tokens)
compactOpusAt.description: Auto-compact an Opus session at this context size. 0 disables it for Opus.

compactHaikuAt.title: Compact Haiku at (tokens)
compactHaikuAt.description: Auto-compact a Haiku session at this context size. 0 disables it for Haiku.

compactFableAt.title: Compact Fable at (tokens)
compactFableAt.description: Auto-compact a Fable session at this context size. 0 disables it for Fable.

compactKeep.title: Keep last messages
compactKeep.description: Recent messages kept word for word; everything older is summarized.

compactInstructions.title: Compact instructions
compactInstructions.description: What the summary should keep or stress (optional), e.g. 'keep the deployment plan and open bugs'.

ultracode.title: Ultracode for the hardest tasks
ultracode.description: For confident Opus/Fable tasks (architecture, unexplained failure, audit, wide migration): suggest names the ultracode keyword in the status line; auto adds it to the prompt (multi-agent workflow: dearer per turn, often done sooner and cheaper overall); off says nothing. In Desktop, Ultracode is the option above Max in the effort picker; this setting automates that switch for the hardest tasks, while the router itself never sends Max.

adapt.title: Learn from your corrections
adapt.description: on: a !tier, !+ or !- override, a /model or /effort change right after a routed prompt and tool-failure escalations shift that kind of task by up to 2 tiers or effort steps, fading over weeks. Kept on this machine only; /router shows it, /router reset clears it.
